name: Batch Messenger
description: Groups Symfony Messenger messages into named collections, shows their progress in a Batch-style admin UI, and can intercept core batch_set() operations and run them as Messenger messages instead.
project_description: Batch Messenger is divided into three pieces of functionality. (1) Base: group Symfony Messenger messages into a named collection by attaching a CollectionItem stamp with a shared collection ID and a unique per-message identifier. (2) UI (optional, on by default): a Reports page at /admin/reports/batch-messenger ("Message sets") plus a toolbar progress bar that show pending/processed counts and a progress bar per collection. (3) Batch API bridge (optional, on by default): intercepts legacy \batch_set() calls via hook_batch_alter() and converts each batch operation into a Messenger message, so operations run off-thread in Messenger workers (in parallel, not single-threaded) while the familiar Batch progress UI is retained. Requires an asynchronous Messenger transport (via the sm module) to actually run operations out of band; otherwise operations execute in the same request. The module is intended as a drop-in replacement for Batch API and can be uninstalled to restore stock behavior (in-progress batches are then lost). Most services are marked @internal.
